prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats’ “Real Alternative” offers a costed, credible, green and liberal programme built on three core principles: Freedom (protecting civil liberties and personal choice), Fairness (opportunity and security for all), and Trust (real accountability and power devolved from Whitehall). A strong environmental thread runs through every policy.

Flagship fairness package funded by a single tax change: introduce a 50% rate only on income above £100,000 (around 1% of taxpayers) to:
- Abolish student tuition and top-up fees.
- Provide free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Replace the unfair Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, cutting the typical household bill by about £450.

Health: put patients before targets; recruit more doctors, nurses and therapists; speed up diagnosis with better use of scanners and evening/weekend capacity; publish diagnostic waits; end charges for eye and dental checks; extend prescription exemptions for serious conditions; guarantee free personal care; strengthen mental health rights; focus on prevention, healthier school food, and ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills: abolish fees and restore grants so no one is deterred from university by debt; cut infant and junior class sizes by redirecting the Child Trust Fund; ensure core subjects are taught by specialist teachers; reduce unnecessary testing; support discipline and special educational needs; create a unified 14–19 diploma blending vocational and academic routes; level up FE funding and invest in modern college facilities; protect free school transport rights.

Crime and liberty: scrap compulsory ID cards and use the savings for 10,000 more police (plus support officers), better tech and less red tape; prioritise serious crime and drugs; expand tough community sentences that cut reoffending; equip prisons to teach skills; create a UK Border Force; defend jury trials and due process; repeal illiberal control-order laws and prosecute terror in open courts; firm but fair asylum with quicker, independent decisions and the right to work; a Single Equality Act and dedicated hate-crime units.

Economy and business: maintain stability and fiscal rules, with NAO scrutiny of the Budget; simplify taxes; raise the stamp duty threshold to £150,000; cut red tape with costed regulation, sunset clauses and streamlined inspections; small business rate relief and site-value reform; abolish the DTI and redirect funds to skills and science; duty to trade fairly; boost tourism. Green fiscal reform: move to a Carbon Tax; stronger incentives for clean homes and vehicles; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no new nuclear.

Pensions and benefits: a Citizen’s Pension with over £100 more per month from age 75, linked to earnings; eight in ten pensioners better off under Local Income Tax; higher, fairer maternity pay for first-time working parents; replace the failing CSA; extend Winter Fuel Payments to severely disabled people; protect pension rights; simplify benefits, cut fraud and error.

Communities and housing: devolve power, merge inspectorates, and put elected local people in charge of services; release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; favour brownfield reuse via VAT reform; manage second homes; protect post offices and universal mail; aim for zero waste with 60% recycling in seven years; embed climate targets in planning.

Europe and the world: opposed the Iraq war; back a managed withdrawal as Iraqi security improves; rebuild multilateralism via the UN, EU, NATO and Commonwealth; support the EU Constitution subject to a UK referendum; prepare to join the euro when conditions are right; reach 0.7% of national income for aid by 2011; push for fair trade and debt relief; lead on climate negotiations (contraction and convergence).

Defence and rural: equip and support overstretched forces; reform procurement and cut low-priority programmes; maintain a minimal nuclear deterrent while advancing global disarmament; tighten arms export controls; fair prices for farmers, CAP reform, a Marine Act, stronger animal welfare, and no commercial GM until proven environmentally safe.

Better government: curb Prime Ministerial power with a War Powers Act; a Civil Service Act; fewer ministers and departments; STV for all elections and a predominantly elected second chamber; votes at 16; greater devolution; an independent BBC regulator; an Environmental Responsibility Act to hold government and business to account.
